question: You need glasses to read a number plate at the required distance. When must you wear them?
options: Only when reversing
Only on motorways
At all times when driving
Only at night
explanation: You MUST be able to read a vehicle number plate, in good daylight, from a distance of 20 metres (or 20.5 metres for old-style number plates). If you need to wear glasses or contact lenses to do this, you MUST wear them at all times while driving. (Highway Code rule 92.)

question: Who is responsible for making sure a 14-year-old front-seat passenger wears a seat belt?
options: The vehicle owner
The passenger themselves
The driver
No one — it is optional at 14
explanation: From 14, passengers are responsible for their own seat belt; below 14 the driver is responsible (rule 100). (Highway Code rule 99.)

question: Who is responsible for ensuring a child under 14 wears a seat belt or correct child restraint in a car?
options: The child’s parent
The driver
The child
The front-seat passenger
explanation: The driver MUST ensure that all children under 14 years of age in cars, vans and other goods vehicles wear seat belts or sit in an approved child restraint where required. (Highway Code rule 100.)

question: Where MUST a rear-facing baby seat NEVER be fitted?
options: In a seat protected by an active frontal airbag
In a seat next to a side airbag
In a seat with a three-point belt
In any rear seat
explanation: A rear-facing baby seat MUST NOT be fitted into a seat protected by an active frontal airbag, as in a crash it can cause serious injury or death to the child. (Highway Code rule 101.)

question: When may you use front or rear fog lights?
options: Only when visibility is seriously reduced
When following another vehicle closely
At night on unlit roads
Whenever it is raining
explanation: You MUST NOT use any lights in a way which would dazzle or cause discomfort to other road users, including pedestrians, cyclists and horse riders, and you MUST NOT use front or rear fog lights unless visibility is seriously reduced. (Highway Code rule 114.)

question: What is the legal minimum tread depth for car tyres across the central three-quarters of the tread and around the entire circumference?
options: 1.0 mm
1.6 mm
2.5 mm
2.0 mm
explanation: 1.6 mm. Source: The Highway Code, Annex 6 (Vehicle maintenance, safety and security).

question: Across what proportion of the tyre’s breadth must the legal minimum tread depth be present on a car?
options: The central three-quarters
The outer edges only
The entire width
The central half
explanation: The central three-quarters. Source: The Highway Code, Annex 6 (Vehicle maintenance, safety and security).

question: Which fluid is it an offence to allow to run out if the system is fitted to the vehicle?
options: Power-steering fluid
Brake fluid
Engine coolant
Windscreen washer fluid
explanation: Windscreen washer fluid. Source: The Highway Code, Annex 6 (Vehicle maintenance, safety and security).

question: You notice excessive exhaust fumes from your vehicle. What should you do?
options: Rev the engine to clear it
Ignore it unless the MOT is due
Add fuel additive at the next fill-up
Have the vehicle checked — driving with a defective exhaust is an offence
explanation: Have the vehicle checked — driving with a defective exhaust is an offence. Source: The Highway Code, Annex 6 (Vehicle maintenance, safety and security).

question: Before a long winter journey, what should you check in addition to fuel and oil?
options: Radio reception
Lights, tyres, coolant and screenwash
Spare fuses only
Air conditioning gas
explanation: Lights, tyres, coolant and screenwash. Source: The Highway Code, Annex 6 (Vehicle maintenance, safety and security).
